newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo soldiers fire rounds in pay dispute.
newsitem.headline: Congo soldiers fire rounds in pay dispute.

text.p: Soldiers of Laurent Kabila's army, angered by a pay dispute, fired off rounds for up to half an hour in the jungle city of Kisangani in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo on Tuesday, residents and local church radio reported.
The soldiers started firing in the crumbling city centre early on Tuesday after some were paid in dollars and others in local "Zaire" currency or not at all, residents said.
"The Tutsis were payed in dollars. For the Rwandans it was a kind of war prime. The Congolese were payed in Zaires or not at all" one senior resident who preferred to remain anonymous said.
Kabila's Rwandan-backed Alliance took power last month after toppling the regime of Mobutu Sese Seko.
Local Church radio, Radio Amani, reported 70 prisoners, some of them "dangerous criminals" escaped from the Kisangani jail during the mayhem.
Kabila's government promised to pay the vast unwieldy civil service by Wednesday for the first time since he took power last month.
Residents of Kisangani were subjected to two rounds of bloody looting in 1991 and 1993 when former dictator Mobutu Sese Seko's army ran amok after a pay dispute.
